1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	World-model reinforcement learning enables sample-efficient learning directly on physical hardware \citep{wu2023daydreamer, hansen2024tdmpc2}. Real robotic tasks demand temporal abstraction: manipulation requires fast reactive grasping alongside slow approach planning, locomotion involves gait phases at different frequencies, and sim-to-real transfer must handle $\dt$ mismatches between simulation and hardware. TAWM \citep{nhu2025tawm} shows that conditioning a world model on step size $\dt$ yields consistent gains within TD-MPC2's MPC framework \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2}. Can the same $\dt$-conditioning bring temporal abstraction to imagination-based actor-critic methods like DreamerV3 \citep{hafner2023dreamerv3}, where policies are trained entirely in imagined rollouts?

We label a configuration as CIVO-positive if and only if (i)~it uses a trained $\dt$-embedding with multi-rate data exposure, and (ii)~NVE exceeds $1.5\times$ with co-occurring entropy collapse. Configurations exhibiting high NVE through other mechanisms (gradient truncation side effects, value anchor pollution) are labeled non-CIVO.

The three false positives are mechanistically distinct from CIVO: (1)~008f seed~0 endpoint eval dip (NVE${=}1.69\times$; corrected-code rerun where eval drops from 342.9 at 95K to 139.5 at 105K, elevating NVE without value overestimation); (2)~frozen-embedding transient exp\_047 (NVE${=}1.71\times$, self-correcting within 20K steps); (3)~frozen-embedding transient exp\_057 (NVE${=}1.88\times$, self-correcting). All three produce NVE $> 1.5\times$ through non-CIVO mechanisms, indicating that the NVE diagnostic detects value overestimation broadly rather than CIVO specifically---a feature rather than a limitation for practitioners monitoring deployment health. The closest sub-threshold case (008f seed~4, NVE${=}1.41\times$) lacks $\dt$-conditioning entirely ($d{=}0$); its elevated NVE reflects transient value noise that self-corrects without the positive feedback loop characteristic of CIVO. The closest above-threshold positive (008d seed~3, NVE${=}1.53\times$) exhibits the full CIVO causal chain: trained $\dt$-embedding, entropy decrease, and evaluation collapse to 14\% of baseline.

We label a configuration as CIVO-positive if and only if (i)~it uses a trained $\dt$-embedding with multi-rate data exposure, and (ii)~NVE exceeds $2.0\times$ with co-occurring evaluation collapse. At $\tau{=}2.0\times$, perfect separation is achieved (AUROC${=}1.000$) with no false positives across $n{=}36$ experiments. 57	Table~\ref{tab:cross_env_civo} reveals that CIVO is complexity-dependent. In multi-joint environments (Walker Walk, 6 joints; Cheetah Run, 6 joints), the trigger configuration reliably induces CIVO (NVE $4.72$--$8.27\times$) while the no-embedding control does not (NVE $\leq 1.69\times$, no value overestimation$^*$), confirming the trained $\dt$-embedding as causal. In contrast, single-joint Cartpole Swingup fails to trigger CIVO even with the identical trained $\dt$-embedding configuration (0/3 seeds, peak NVE $0.06\times$; exp\_061), and the no-embedding control confirms this is not a masking effect: trigger ($236.3$) and control ($244.8$) achieve comparable performance ($-65\%$ vs.\ $-64\%$ relative to baseline), indicating that the performance degradation stems from the subsample$+$$H{=}8$ configuration itself rather than $\dt$-embedding---the embedding neither triggers CIVO nor causes additional damage in single-DOF dynamics. This establishes a scope boundary: CIVO is specific to multi-joint locomotion under imagination-based training with temporal conditioning, not a general pathology of $\dt$-conditioned world models.

7	\paragraph{Causal role of embedding training.}
8	The three-way ablation (trained/frozen/removed $\dt$-embedding; Table~\ref{tab:causal_ablation}) disambiguates two hypotheses: CIVO could arise from the architectural presence of a $\dt$-conditioning pathway, or specifically from learned $\dt$-specific representations shaped by gradient flow. Since frozen embeddings participate in the forward pass identically to trained ones yet do not trigger CIVO (0/13 frozen or removed controls vs.\ 6/7 trained, $p < 0.001$; NVE ${\leq}\,0.53\times$ in all four cross-environment frozen seeds), the vulnerability lies in what the embedding \emph{learns}---near-antipodal representations (Figure~\ref{fig:cosine_similarity}; temporal dynamics in \S\ref{sec:cosine_temporal}) that create exploitable structure through environment-dependent pathways (reward fidelity degradation in Walker, alternative transmission in Cheetah; Table~\ref{tab:rssm_fidelity})---rather than in conditioning architecture per se. For world-model RL systems using DreamerV3's RSSM, this suggests that auxiliary conditioning signals whose gradient flow touches the dynamics model require fidelity guarantees matching the model's prediction accuracy; without such guarantees, learned conditioning creates exploitable structure that imagination-based critics cannot self-correct.
